scores.name: display-lut
scores.notes:
The placement is right: a display-referred 33³ RGBA16F tap after renderOutput, applied once in the post quad that the app already owns. Grade off gives a byte-identical graph and zero cost, and tone-mapping.ts is untouched. It is the smallest change set. Weak points:
- Storage is clamped to [0,1] at the nodes, so values above 1 in cubes and graded nodes clip before interpolation instead of per pixel.
- The two-sided power contrast has infinite end slopes for c < 1, which expands 8-bit steps in the darks.
- The wheels are cramped at 202 px.
- Interop has a measured flaw. The own-size exact path only holds while every control is neutral; any control moved composites the look at 33³. I re-ran the scratchpad resample-cubes.mjs: Adobe's 21³ cubes resampled to 33³ are off by up to 14.9 LSB, 22.7 % of 8-bit outputs change on average, and 32³ cubes are off by 26 LSB. So nudging one slider on top of a loaded look makes the image visibly jump.
- No draft bake while dragging.
What it does well: the RGC gamut guard, the bundled parser that handled all 265 Adobe files, and the grade-output.test.ts texture-flag test.

scores.name: unified
scores.notes:
The colourist's dream structure: grade in log, then the output transform, so HDR gains and warm highlights roll off through the shoulder. The residual storage, Canopy Log and q-scaling are clever and measured. It fails the brief in several places:
- At the Film preset the user's approved Film Warm look is not bit-exact: up to 1.3 LSB, 1.5-8 % of codes change, and the sky slope error reaches 8 %.
- Because the default is a non-identity grade, a 3D tap plus 3 log2 runs for every viewer at all times, with the phone cost unmeasured. That breaks 'compile out when off' and 'no performance loss'.
- 'Grade off' now also removes the film's contrast, saturation and split, so it no longer shows today's look.
- The grade vanishes with Shoulder, AgX or the tone-stage switch.
- Screenshot .cube files cannot be folded in (14-25 LSB through the inverse display transform), so it needs a second display-referred look slot with an EOTF/OETF round trip: two LUT stages.
- 1D-shaper cubes are rejected.
- It rewrites tone-mapping.ts and config, and needs 32 slots.
Worth taking: powC1 and kink-free maths in general, compare against a reference LUT, 'export look for photos', and the JS film twin for tests.

scores.name: editor-first
scores.notes:
Same placement and compile-out guarantee as display-lut (zero cost off, one tap on), with better maths and interop:
- Storage is unclamped half and the canvas clamps per pixel, so values above 1 in cubes interpolate as authored.
- The gamut compression is input-relative tanh and C1 at its threshold. It leaves already-saturated canopy alone until the grade pushes further.
- Contrast below 1 becomes a linear fade, so there are no infinite end slopes.
- The shadow tint keeps true black black.
- Imports use an integer-refined lattice, k·(N−1)+1. I re-ran resample-refine2.mjs: 21→41 within 0.10 LSB on all 90 cubes, 16→46 and 32→63 within 0.06. This is the only design where a loaded .cube stays 1:1 while controls move on top of it.
- The stride-2 draft bake equals a 17³ texture (0.09 LSB), so drags stay at about 1-2 ms of worker time.
- Usability is best: Resolve-style relative wheels, tabs, A/B, undo semantics, peek mode on phones, a scroll fallback, keyboard isolation, and Paste values that also accepts .cube text.
Costs: the biggest scope (about 11 modules), a binder refactor in main.ts, LookState coupling tone and grade, a 'Neutral' preset that switches the curve to Shoulder, imported lattices up to 63³ (2 MiB) with phone tap cost unmeasured, and a gamma `y>0 ? pow : y` kink at 0.

blocking_issues:
1. Path B (DoF and EDL off) is untested while compiled in. The frame goes through RenderPipeline with a PassNode target (HalfFloat + DepthTexture, about 18 MB at 2.25 Mpx, kept after first use) instead of renderer.render's frameBufferTarget.
   - Measure the delta with the stopped-loop, paired-baseline timestamp method on WebGPU and ?webgl before shipping.
   - Fall back to a film-slot tap for path B only if the delta exceeds about 0.02 ms.
   - Already verified: release() frees only dofNode and the EDL rtt (depth-of-field.ts:91-105), so scenePass.getTextureNode() stays valid as the path-B effectNode. RenderPipeline._update (RenderPipeline.js:190-226) puts toneMapping and outputColorSpace into the context when outputColorTransform is false, so renderOutput() with no arguments stays correct across film slot changes.

2. The gamma stage `y > 0 ? y^(1/γ) : y` has a slope discontinuity at 0 (pow slope 0 or ∞), which puts a kink inside the first lattice cell. Negative lift reaches it. Replace it with a C1 linear extension (powC1) and test that continuity.

3. Presets must not change the approved look.
   - 'Neutral' switches the tone curve to Shoulder and exposure to 1. That is not a neutral grade, and it recompiles the film slot.
   - Moving #toneExposure out of Tone & colour changes the existing panel and the Copy values dump.
   - Keep the film owned by Tone & colour, and limit v1 presets, snapshots and undo to grade + LUT.

4. Refined import lattices (41³ to 63³, 0.55-2 MiB) and a 65³ option have an unmeasured 3D-tap cost on phones and WebGL2. Measure 33/41/63 on desktop and one phone. If the cost is high, keep a 33 resample fallback that shows a visible 'not 1:1' warning.

5. Compile-in while the editor is open at identity runs an identity LUT.
   - Measure the hardware filter-weight flip rate (estimated 1-3 % of pixels by one level) and the compile-in hitch per backend.
   - Never decide compile-in or compile-out on an 'input' event.
   - Re-evaluate on the design panel closing, not only on the section toggle.

6. Unclamped half storage relies on the canvas clamping. Verify that the WebGPU bgra8/rgba8unorm canvas and the WebGL2 RGBA8 default framebuffer clamp on both backends, and that NaN can never enter: the parser rejects non-numbers, and the bake must not create NaN.

7. The canvas is 8-bit with no dither anywhere, so shadow-stretching grades band in dark greens. Measure on a dark canopy and haze gradient before a non-neutral grade ships. Decide on an optional TPDF dither that is compiled only with the tap and off at identity.

8. Canvas readback (toBlob for the frame grab, createImageBitmap for the histogram) must run in the same task right after a render, or WebGPU returns a blank frame.
   - Verify this on both backends.
   - Cut the histogram from v1 unless its stall measures under 1 ms.

9. The binder refactor (bindDesignSlider, bindSeg and bindEffectToggle returning {set, get}) must keep every existing caller's boot behaviour byte-identical, including the single initial apply. Prove it with an old-vs-new shader hash and a 0-pixel canvas diff at defaults against 81ccfab.

10. The scope is too large for one step: about 11 modules plus peek mode, the scroll fallback, restore-session and cube-text paste. Land it in stages:
    - first, the pure maths with node --test, the tap, and compile-out;
    - then the widgets;
    - then the extras.

11. 1D-only cubes 'applied through the lattice' are not 1:1 for steep log-to-video curves at 33 nodes per axis. Show the warning prominently, or refuse such files.

12. Commit on top of the actual HEAD 81ccfab, not the 2def41d the task text names, and leave .claude/launch.json uncommitted.

scores.name: display-lut
scores.notes: Best base. Every three r185 claim it relies on checks out in the code. (1) With outputColorTransform=false, RenderPipeline._update puts toneMapping and outputColorSpace into the context and wraps the whole outputNode (RenderPipeline.js:214-219). renderOutput() without arguments then reads them (RenderOutputNode.js:119-121). The pipeline still rebuilds on a renderer.toneMapping change (:181-193), so film slot switches keep working. The only reader of context.outputColorSpace is ColorSpaceNode's OUTPUT placeholder (ColorSpaceNode.js:77), so flipping the flag changes nothing upstream. (2) texture3D(tex, null, 0).sample(uvw): clone() passes levelNode (TextureNode.js:920), so this emits textureSampleLevel/textureLod. Texture3DNode ignores updateMatrix (Texture3DNode.js:115). (3) The lutNode.value swap works: the setter and getter delegate through referenceNode (TextureNode.js:186-207), NodeSampledTexture.update rebinds (:54-66), and Bindings bumps the bind group on a generation change. customCacheKey is the node id (Node.js:470), so a size swap should not recompile. (4) select().uniformFlow() emits a ternary (ConditionalNode.js:146-158). (5) RenderPipeline is exported from three/webgpu (Three.WebGPU.js:14). (6) Data3DTexture defaults to Nearest (Data3DTexture.js:56,66). Grade off: the graph and path B are today's, byte for byte, so it costs zero. The grade works with every curve and with the stage off. setGrade does not call release(), so the DoF targets survive a toggle. Weaknesses: it clamps to [0,1] at the lattice nodes and in the export, and it resamples foreign-N looks onto 33 as soon as a control moves (a jump of up to about 15 LSB per editor-first's measurement). Four 95 px wheels at 202 px are cramped. The exposure trim is invisible to the before/after split and does nothing with the stage off. Path B routing is unmeasured. Minor factual slip shared with the pipeline reader: toneMappingModeOf is not hard-coded to 100..115, it scales with FILM_PART_ORDER.length (tone-mapping.ts:209).

scores.name: editor-first
scores.notes: Same placement and tap as display-lut; the r185 claims are verified the same way, and .sample(uvw).level(0) on a base texture3D node is fine. Its real contributions, all measured: (a) The refined import lattice k(N-1)+1 (21->41, 16->46, 32->63, cap 65). This keeps Adobe's 21^3 cubes within 0.10 LSB while editor controls are composited on top, against 15-26 LSB when resampled to 33. (b) Unclamped half storage, with the unorm canvas clamping per pixel. This matters for 72 of 98 Adobe cubes, which carry values above 1, and gives exact hard clips. (c) Input-relative gamut compression, so a control that just leaves neutral does not desaturate canopy that was already saturated. (d) The linear fade form for contrast below 1. (e) Relative-drag wheels like Resolve's, a phone peek mode, and a selectable-textarea Copy fallback for plain-HTTP phones. Scope creep is heavy: a LookState that also owns the film/tone controls, a rewrite of every binder to return handles, #toneExposure moved into the grade, Film Warm/Neutral presets that switch the tone curve, localStorage persistence of looks and cube blobs, a histogram via createImageBitmap (an unmeasured readback stall on WebGPU), stride-2 draft bakes plus a fill pass, a manual scroll fallback on touch canvases, and Paste values that also accepts .cube text. Larger refined textures (41^3-63^3) and the histogram are the extra performance risk. It shares the transferable-buffer reuse hazard with display-lut: identityTexels or the current image.data must never be transferred.

scores.name: unified
scores.notes: Clever engineering: a residual LUT, a Canopy Log shaper with a C1 toe, homogeneous q-extrapolation for HDR, and grading in scene-linear so highlights roll off through the shoulder. The TSL claims hold: the tone fn signature, texture3D level kept, the value swap, a plain QuadMesh on path B. Problems: (1) It replaces film tone and split with the LUT, so the shipped default (contrast 1, saturation 1.17, split 2) always runs the LUT. The default look changes by up to 1.3 LSB, with 1.5-8 % of codes moving, and needs sign-off. The default frame pays one 3D tap plus 3 log2, and nothing compiles out at the user's settings. (2) The slope error along the sky gradient is 8 % at the default preset, a contouring risk on the shipped look over an 8-bit canvas without dither. (3) Grade off is not 'film ungraded': it removes the film's own saturation and split, so the switch changes the shipped look. (4) Screenshot .cube files cannot be absorbed (14-25 LSB), which forces a second display-referred Look slot: two LUT stages and an EOTF/OETF round trip, which kills the 'one place' argument. (5) Grade and look exist only with the film curve and the stage on. (6) The largest churn: film rows removed from Tone & colour, config moved into grade.preset, Copy values reshaped, a new panel that hides the HUD. Strong pro grades interpolate worse (4.2 LSB full cube) because 38 % of cells lie above diffuse white. Keep the C1-everywhere principle (powC1, vibrance without max/min) and the later 'look for photos' export idea.

blocking_issues:
1. Transferable buffer reuse. The main thread 'sends the old buffer back' to the worker. That buffer must never be the cached identityLattice(n). It must also never be an array that is still lut.image.data and not yet uploaded. If it is, the cache or the texture data becomes a detached ArrayBuffer, and later identity uploads or re-uploads fail or upload zero bytes. Fix: copy the identity per texture, or keep a pool that excludes the cached and current arrays. Test this with the pure scheduler.

2. Clamping at the lattice nodes. bake step 4 clamps to [0,1] and serializeCube clamps on export. This turns the authored >1 values of imported cubes (72 of 98 Adobe creative cubes) into softened knees inside cells, and blurs hard clips from gain or highlight grades. Store unclamped half and let the 8-bit unorm canvas clamp per pixel; export unclamped.

3. Look resampling jump. A 16/21/32/64-point look is uploaded exactly at its own N only while every control is neutral. Touching any control resamples it onto 33, a visible jump measured at up to about 15 LSB, with 22-41 % of 8-bit outputs changing. Use the refined lattice k(N-1)+1 (cap 65) in both cases.

4. Path B (DoF and EDL off) routed through RenderPipeline is unmeasured. Measure PassNode RT + quad against renderer.render with the stopped-loop per-render timestamp method on WebGPU and ?webgl. Also measure the compile-in hitch when the section opens, on desktop and a phone. Take the film-slot fallback only if the delta exceeds about 0.02 ms. Document in viewer/CLAUDE.md that ?dof=0&edl=0 is the no-post baseline only while the grade is compiled out.

5. Compile-out proof. depth-of-field.ts switches from PostProcessing to RenderPipeline and gains the chain/applyOutput split. With the grade off, prove that the post-quad shader source hash and a canvas capture equal 81ccfab's (0 differing pixels) on both backends. Prove 0 rebuilds during 10 s drags on every widget with a build counter. Prove that a texture size swap triggers no recompile; the cache key is the node id, so none is expected.

6. Identity rules. isIdentityGrade must treat look amount 0, or a cube within 1e-5 of identity, as no look. Pucks under 0.02 must snap to exactly 0. The compile decision is taken only on commit, toggle, or section open and close, never on 'input'.

7. Exposure semantics. A grade 'exposure trim' on renderer.toneMappingExposure does nothing with the tone stage off (NoToneMapping skips the fn) and is invisible to the before/after split. Either drop it from v1, or compute baseExposure x 2^trim in one function shared with the Tone & colour slider, and label or disable it when the stage is off.

8. Frame (grade off) capture. The extra out-of-loop render must do the same nodeFrame and info bookkeeping as the loop. The drawImage or toBlob must run in the same task as the render (WebGPU current texture; WebGL without preserveDrawingBuffer). Verify a non-blank, grade-bypassed frame on both backends.

9. Keyboard and touch. Widget keydown must stopPropagation, because window (keyboard-navigation.ts:168) and document (main.ts:880, 2101, 2998) all listen in the bubble phase. Escape should blur the widget. touch-action:none and pointer capture go on the widget canvases only, so the sheet still scrolls elsewhere. The split handle must stay in the strip that is visible above the 64vh phone sheet. Test on a real phone over dev:https and over plain-HTTP WebGL2.

10. Housekeeping. Commit on top of 81ccfab, not the 2def41d the task text named. Leave .claude/launch.json uncommitted. The pure modules (grade-model, grade-bake, cube-format) must import nothing from three or the DOM and must use .ts imports, so npm run bench:verify runs them. The .cube parser must accept CRLF, tabs, comments between keywords, signed and exponent DOMAIN values, and LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE. It must check the N^3 count, and reject 1D and shaper files with a message instead of misreading them.
